title: Best Recruiting Agencies for Startups: July 2026
summary: Our July 2026 ranking of the best recruiting agencies for startups. Compare top options for early-stage hiring, executive search, and fractional support.
body_markdown:
For a seed or Series A team without a dedicated recruiter, choosing among[recruiting agencies for startups](https://www.dover.com/) means weighing a real tradeoff: pay a traditional agency 15-30% of salary per hire, manage the process yourself, or hire full-time before the volume supports it. This guide breaks down the top options, what each costs, and where each fits.


**TLDR:**


-


Traditional recruiting agencies charge 15-30% of salary; fractional recruiting agencies can average $4K-$7K per hire.


-


Match your agency choice to your stage: fractional recruiting agencies for early-to-mid roles, retained firms for executive searches.


-


Executive search firms like Riviera Partners and Korn Ferry operate on retained fees of 25-30% of salary with 3-6 month timelines.


-


Referral-driven models can surface passive candidates, though quality and cost vary by firm and role type.


-


Some tools pair a free ATS with on-demand recruiting support at $75-$125/hour instead of fixed retainers.


## Dover: Best Overall Startup Recruiting (#1)


[Dover](https://www.dover.com/recruiters) takes the top spot as the best recruiting solution for startups in 2026. Unlike a traditional agency, Dover combines a free hiring platform with on-demand recruiting services.


In one package, you get free AI-powered tools, multi-channel sourcing, and a marketplace of fractional recruiters who step in or out based on your hiring needs. This blend of software and service, built for startups, makes Dover a one-stop shop for companies looking to scale their team.


### What Key Features and Benefits Make Dover #1


-


**Free ATS and Career Pages:** A full-featured, free ATS with an AI-generated careers page and job descriptions, so you can track applicants and organize your pipeline from day one.


-


**AI Candidate Scoring:** Dover’s **AI-powered resume scoring** shortlists the most promising candidates automatically, so your time goes to the applicants who matter most.


-


**Integrated Sourcing Tools:** Dover’s[sourcing extension](https://www.dover.com/sourcing) helps you find and contact candidates quickly, with personalized outreach built in.


-


**One-Click Job Board Posting:** Post a role to 100+ job boards in a single click, without manually submitting to each site.


-


**Employee Referrals System:** A built-in **employee referrals system** lets team members submit referrals and tracks those candidates through the same pipeline.


-


**Marketplace of Fractional Recruiters:** When you need extra help, Dover’s marketplace of[vetted recruiters](https://www.dover.com/recruiters) can step in on a flexible, part-time basis as an extension of your team.


Dover also serves as the infrastructure layer that many fractional recruiting agencies are built on. When a fractional recruiting agency needs an ATS, sourcing tools, and candidate management in one place, Dover is the system they build their workflow around. Every recruiter in the marketplace comes with real published reviews, fill-rate data, and cost-per-hire history from prior searches, so founders can compare recruiter performance before committing to a search.


### Considerations


The core platform is free, and the fractional recruiter service is pay-as-you-go. Most companies spend around[~$4k-$7k per hire on Dover](https://www.dover.com/pricing) , compared to the[headhunter fee rates](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/h/headhunter.asp) of 15-30% of salary that traditional agencies charge.


Dover shows the historical cost-per-hire for each recruiter in its marketplace, so you know what to expect before you start. For a deeper look at what recruiters typically charge, see our guide on[fractional recruiter costs](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiter-costs) .


### **When to choose Dover**


If you’re a seed or Series A startup without full-time recruiting staff, Dover offers a cost-effective path: from job postings and candidate tracking to on-demand recruiter support, without the retainers of a traditional agency.


## **Paraform: On-Demand Recruiter Marketplace (Rank #2)**


Coming in at #2 is Paraform, a marketplace that connects startups with independent recruiters on demand. You post a role, a pool of vetted freelance recruiters compete to fill it, and Paraform provides coordination tools, though interviewing and final decisions stay with the hiring team.


### **Key benefits**


-


Speed: Recruiters are motivated to perform well as they get paid per hire or interview milestone. And as a result, you quickly get multiple independent recruiters sourcing candidates for you.


-


Affordable: Paraform charges a success fee only when a hire is made, typically around 20%-25% of the candidate’s first-year base salary, though final terms may vary.


Paraform is relatively new (founded in 2023) and recruiter quality can vary.[Dover](https://www.dover.com/recruiters) provides performance data upfront, and unlike Paraform, includes a built-in ATS so you’re not managing candidates outside the system. For a side-by-side look, see the[Dover vs. Paraform comparison](https://www.dover.com/compare/dover-vs-paraform) .


### **When to Choose Paraform**


Paraform fits early-stage teams filling high-demand roles fast without locking into a single firm. It fits early-stage teams filling high-demand roles like engineering or sales.


## **Riviera Partners: Tech Executive Search (#3)**


Ranking #3 is Riviera Partners, a premier executive search firm specializing in tech leadership (CTO, VP of Engineering, Head of Product) with a two-decade record placing executives at venture-backed startups.


-


Deep executive network: Their team focuses solely on tech and product leadership searches. Riviera acts as an extension of your company’s leadership team. They will refine the role requirements with you, headhunt passive candidates, and thoroughly vet each candidate.


-


Data-driven approach. Their internal database and machine learning models help them find candidates with the right domain knowledge and success in similar roles.


-


Reputation and reach: Trusted by top VCs and CEOs, Riviera is often investor-recommended. Their presence in major hubs like Silicon Valley, NYC, and London expands your talent access.


Riviera operates on a retained basis, with fees governed by[retained-search structures](https://cowenpartners.com/the-two-types-of-executive-search-firms-fees/) that are commonly calculated as a percentage of first-year compensation. Riviera’s current guidance indicates that well-run technology executive searches often take six to eight weeks, while some more complex searches may take eight to 12 weeks.


### **When to choose Riviera Partners**


If your startup needs a key executive and a mis-hire carries real organizational risk, Riviera is worth considering. Most seed-stage startups won’t reach this level until Series A or B, when investor backing makes the retained fee structure more viable.


## **Hunt Club: Referral-Driven Recruiting (#4)**


At #4, we have Hunt Club, which connects startups to talent through a network of 20,000+ industry experts who make warm referrals. The model surfaces passive candidates that job boards rarely reach, and their recruiters manage the process end-to-end.


-


**Referral-driven sourcing:** Hunt Club draws on a network of 20,000+ industry experts who refer candidates from their own circles, surfacing[passive talent](https://cvviz.com/recruitment-statistics/) that standard job boards rarely reach.


-


**Broad candidate reach:** The referral model gives access to a large pool of potential candidates and tends to surface stronger fits for roles where domain experience or cultural match matters most.


-


**Full-service support:** Hunt Club’s recruiters manage outreach, referral tracking, and interview coordination the way a traditional search firm would, so founders are not running the process alone.


Hunt Club serves clients from early-stage startups to larger companies across both executive and non-executive roles, so startup-specific focus can vary. Pricing follows a traditional percentage-of-salary or flat-fee model.


### **When to choose Hunt Club**


Hunt Club fits startups hiring for roles where domain experience or cultural fit matters most and where a passive-candidate referral approach is worth the search firm pricing.


## **Korn Ferry: Global Executive Search (#5)**


Rounding out our list at #5 is Korn Ferry, one of the largest global executive search firms. If your startup needs a C-suite hire or a search that spans geographies, Korn Ferry has the infrastructure to run it.


-


**Scale and reach:** Korn Ferry’s talent analytics platform draws on over 5 billion workforce and talent data points, supported by a global network of consultants and researchers.


-


**Specialized teams:** They organize by function and industry, so a tech startup works with technology practice experts who can tap into a worldwide network of contacts.


-


**Assessment tools:** Proprietary methods cover leadership style, competencies, and culture fit, often producing detailed candidate reports on each person’s strengths and gaps.


Korn Ferry operates on a[retained basis at 25-30% of salary](https://perelson.com/executive-search-pricing-understanding-payment-models-and-partnership-structures/) . For early-stage startups, that fee is hard to support unless the hire is high-profile, and some note that personal attention can feel thinner than a boutique search.


### **When to choose Korn Ferry**


Korn Ferry makes sense when the hire is high-profile, global, or both, a Series C company hiring a General Manager for EMEA, for instance. Most early-stage startups won’t need them until they’ve scaled considerably, but the firm’s global reach is hard to match at that level.


## **Picking the Right Recruiting Partner**


Each option has its strengths, here’s how they map to stage and need:


**Service** **Best For** **What You Get**


**Dover** Early-stage startups All-in-one hiring platform + on-demand fractional recruiters; affordable and flexible


**Paraform** Fast, flexible hiring for startups Marketplace of recruiters; quick fills, but more founder involvement for later stages.


**Riviera / Korn Ferry** Executive-level hires (Series A-B, if funded) Premium agencies with deep networks; ideal for VP/C-suite searches


**Hunt Club** Startups that need mid-to-senior-level, passive candidates Referral-driven recruiting; access to vetted, hard-to-reach talent


In practice, many startups use a combination of these approaches over time, shifting models as hiring volume and role seniority change. The key is to be aware of what each offers, what you need, and where each shines to help you reach your goals, on budget.


## **How Dover Stands Out Among Recruiting Agencies for Startups**


Most recruiting agencies for startups force a choice: a standalone ATS with no human support, or a traditional agency working outside your tools. Dover removes that tradeoff by combining a[free ATS](https://www.dover.com/ats) with a vetted network of fractional recruiters who work directly inside your hiring pipeline.


Dover also functions as the infrastructure layer that many fractional recruiting agencies are built on. Every recruiter in the marketplace carries a published track record: real reviews, fill-rate data, and cost-per-hire figures from prior searches, so founders can compare performance before a search begins.


For startups comparing recruiting agencies, Dover covers the full range from first hire through Series B, with no retainer required and cost-per-hire averaging $2,000 to $7,000.


## **FAQs**


### **Dover vs. Paraform for early-stage startup hiring: which model actually fits?**


Dover gives you an integrated ATS plus a dedicated fractional recruiter who works as part of your team, while Paraform sends your role to multiple independent recruiters competing on placement. If you want a single recruiter who builds context on your company over time, Dover fits better; if you want maximum candidate volume fast and are comfortable managing coordination yourself, Paraform works for urgent, well-defined roles.


### **Can I manage multiple recruiting agencies through a single system without losing track of candidate submissions and fees?**


Yes. Dover’s Agency Portal gives founders a centralized dashboard showing every candidate submitted by external agencies, their current status, and associated fees, so you can run contingency firms in parallel without placement-fee disputes that arise when two vendors find the same candidate.


### **What information do I need before engaging a startup recruiting agency?**


At minimum: a clear job description, a defined compensation range covering salary and equity, a realistic hiring timeline, and a ranked list of must-have versus nice-to-have qualifications. A compelling pitch on why a strong candidate should leave their current role matters just as much, since recruiters are selling your opportunity to passive candidates, and the clearer that pitch is from day one, the faster a search moves.


## **Final Thoughts on Recruiting Agencies for Startups**


Choosing among[recruiting agencies for startups](https://www.dover.com/) comes down to your stage and what the hire requires. Fractional models cover most seed-to-Series B searches well; retained firms make sense when the role is VP-level or above and a mis-hire carries real risk. Dover sits at the intersection: a free ATS paired with on-demand fractional recruiters, so founders can keep cost-per-hire in check without a dedicated recruiting team.
